title: Before HBO’s The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
description: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media. Like with many Hollywood productions, The Last of Us had a tumultuous, long development period as a movie before it was ultimately abandoned in favor of what is now a hit series. While not everyone agrees with the creative departures from the source material for the TV series on HBO, it's undeniably a success and one of HBO's biggest hits lately. Let's look back at how The Last of Us originated as a movie and run through the key developments that led to it becoming a TV show. The original movie pitch People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture." This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films. That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success). This was a year after The Last of Us came out in 2013. It was a hot property, as the game was a critical and a commercial success for Naughty Dog and Sony. With Sony also owning and operating its own film studio, all the synergies were there for Sony to make a Last of Us film. Neil Druckmann, who directed The Last of Us game, confirmed in 2014 that the movie would adapt the story of The Last of Us, as opposed to branching off in some other way. At the time, Druckmann said the movie would "take into account the unique properties of film," but he stressed it was early days and the team hadn't yet mapped out how it would condense the game's…

description: Are you intrigued by the existence of Sanzhani in The Blood of Dawnwalker? These beings, a cross between a moth and a pixie, are fairies who live in small burrows underground. Don’t let their diminutive size fool you, because they’re quite tricky and mischievous, too. However, if you can help them out, you might just receive the most important resource in the game: Time. Our guide has all the information that you need. We discuss the Good Home quest and Letters to Lunka quest. Here’s the kicker: You won’t be able to see any of them from the get-go. Instead, you have to complete a prerequisite quest called Good Home. From there, you’ll be able to search for the remaining four fairies. A map that shows the locations of the Sanzhani fairies and their respective quests. Good Home: Heile, Tonis, and the ruins of Oghasti First, you have to tackle The Blood of Dawnwalker Good Home quest. Make your way to the quest marker in Svartrau Outskirts and look for a flowerbed with glowing moths. Follow the glowing insects to the next flowerbed and continue onward until you see a small opening. Crawl through the opening to arrive at a small underground hovel called the Yawning Burrow. There, you’ll meet a little girl named Heile. Heile says that she’s from Oghasti, an abandoned village to the south. Make your way there and investigate her old home. title: NBA 2K’s Best Mode Is Even Better This Year
description: NBA 2K has long been the standard-bearer for high-quality sports games. It's the pinnacle that other series like Madden, FC, and even the oft-beloved MLB The Show aspire to emulate in whatever ways their respective sports allow. That's not to say it gets everything right, but it often feels like the team at Visual Concepts is competing against itself. It creates trends; it doesn't chase them. That's always been most obvious in The City, the series' social PvPvE hub and the lifeblood of the game's community. Though some other parts of the game are more uneven with this year's entry, The City proves that if you only plan to play one sports game this year, NBA 2K27 is the way to go. The City is where players can meet up for basketball games of varying sweat levels, buy cosmetics, and complete live-service challenges--it is the center of NBA 2K27's solar system. This hub is thoughtfully attached to the single-player MyCareer mode at the proverbial hip, and this pairing offers more enjoyable and immersive things to do as a tandem than most other sports games taken in their totality. This year, The City makes several smart changes. At the core of it all is the long-awaited ability to import custom women characters into the mode. Aesthetically, this is a nice change that lets the hub world better reflect real-life streetball communities--it's always been true that women have existed in these spaces in real life, so they should be included in NBA 2K, too. However, this positive change does come with a frustrating caveat: The MyCareer mode doesn't account for them, thereby siloing these women avatars into The City exclusively. Plus, this requires anyone who wants to run around in The City as a woman to create a second avatar as a man if they want to go into MyCareer's story mode. So as awesome as this all is to see, it also feels like a frustrating half-step forward. Finally bringing women avatars into The City makes for a more diverse and dynamic social space. New…

title: Who Should Receive Farkas’ Ring In The Blood Of Dawnwalker – The Ring Guide
description: Are you having doubts as to who should receive Farkas' Ring in The Blood of Dawnwalker? Farkas, the jester for Mad Khan Bakir, has a deal for you. Of course, it's up to you if you want to push through with the idea or if you feel like you should renege on it. But if you change your mind, you'll have to find someone who'll take the item. In This Article The Ring quest - Should Farkas or someone else get the ring? What happens if you give the ring to Farkas? Who else can take the ring? Anca Bakr-Erga, the Uriash Matriarch Sanzhani Tsarina The Ring quest - Should Farkas or someone else get the ring? The Ring in The Blood of Dawnwalker is actually a follow-up mission. Your main objective is to defeat the Mad Khan, Bakir, as part of the Lunar Game quest. Here’s a brief rundown: Once you’ve angered Bakir, his jester, Farkas, will approach you and hatch a plan. This leads to the Lunar Game quest where you have to become the sole survivor of a deadly maze. Farkas just wants you to bring him an item, a ring with an amethyst that’s supposed to be a family heirloom. If you can enter Bakir’s treasure room and beat him there, you’ll find said item--also known as the Ring with the Purple Eye--on one of the shelves. Well, this seems ominous. What happens if you give the ring to Farkas? At first glance, you might just want to hand over the ring to Farkas in The Blood of Dawnwalker. If you talk to him, he’ll say that Bakir gravely abused his younger brother, and the ring might be the only thing that could reverse his condition. That seems like a noble cause. There’s just one problem: The ring has demonic runes inscribed on it, and Farkas has absolutely no clue about arcane rituals. Giving it to him is going to be a huge risk. Still, if you decide to do it, just know that things won’t bode well for Farkas and his brother, as you’ll find out much later at the end of the game. Do you trust this fella? Who else can take the ring? Of course, you can also choose not to give the item to…

description: The Lunar Game in The Blood of Dawnwalker is a major quest that you eventually receive if you’ve been targeting Bakir’s operations in the region. If you keep at it with certain activities, such as freeing prisoners from pillories, ransacking distilleries, and eliminating headhunters, Bakir will become so irate. Shortly thereafter, his jester, Farkas, will approach you with a plan to join a contest. Our guide has several tips to help you survive the night. In This Article Bakir’s fall - The Lunar Game Preparations and meeting the competitors Don’t blow your cover The trap and the riddle A feast for champions Bakir boss fight The Lunar Game: Bakir’s death and the treasure room Bakir’s fall - The Lunar Game Think of the Lunar Game in The Blood of Dawnwalker as a PvPvE battle royale segment of sorts. It takes place in Bakir’s stronghold known as the Lunar Manor. Basically, Coen will start with just low-tier equipment. You won’t have access to your high-end gear, so you have to look for upgrades in the fortress. All the while, you must take out hostile creatures and human combatants. Bakir does not know Coen is one of the participants. If you want to succeed, you have to avoid using vampiric powers, as doing so would make Bakir suspicious. Farkas might be a jester, but he's not clowning around. Preparations and meeting the competitors The tournament itself starts at dusk, but Farkas suggests arriving early so you can meet the other participants. Ideally, you should accept Farkas’ invitation during the afternoon--i.e. Daytime at 5x Time Segments. This gives you 3x Time Segments to stymy your opponents and look for allies. title: All Endings In The Blood Of Dawnwalker, Including Both Secret Endings
description: Are you curious about all the endings in The Blood of Dawnwalker? Your journey across the fields, bogs, and castles of Vale Sangora has to come to a close some time, whether you manage to do it in 30 days or not. Our guide has all the information that you could ever want but, due to the topic that we’ll discuss, do expect several major spoilers. In This Article The Blood of Dawnwalker endings, epilogues, and extras Secret ending: The Hero They Deserve Secret ending: Together Forever Bad ending: Your Family Is Sacrificed Good ending: In the Nick of Time Good ending: The Folk Hero Good endings: The Patricide and The Knyazmaker Douchebag ending: The Turncoat Epilogue 1: Things Will Be Different Now Epilogue 2: Character Fates Post-credits scene: Present-day Bonus ending: What happens if you beat Brencis during the prologue? The Blood of Dawnwalker endings, epilogues, and extras There are multiple endings in The Blood of Dawnwalker, and all of them can be obtained in a single playthrough, especially if you keep backup saves. We’re going to start off with those that can be achieved before even reaching Castle Greifberg, the citadel of the vampire lord Brencis. Then, we look into how the campaign concludes for Coen, whether he has allies or not. Finally, we talk about the epilogue scenes woven akin to a medieval tapestry. Secret ending: The Hero They Deserve You can get this ending by leaving Vale Sangora via the aptly named Coward’s Path. You won’t rescue your family. You won’t bother with Brencis. You’ll just try to start a new life. We’re reminded of other secret/joke endings where the protagonist just avoids all conflict, such as those from Far Cry 4 and Far Cry 6. Thanks for nuthin'. Secret ending: Together Forever This secret ending in The Blood of Dawnwalker can be unlocked as part of the Home Sweet Home quest. Normally, you should figure out that you’re stuck in a time loop so you can make your escape. But, if Coen keeps pushing onward without facing his guilt,…

title: A Lot Of New Games Released On Steam Today, But This One Has Wormed Its Way Into My Heart
description: Would I still love working from home if I was a worm? Turns out the answer is a resounding yes, and I never would have made this crucial discovery if it hadn't been for Worming From Home. What's Worming From Home? Oh I am so glad you asked. In the midst of September's glut of new releases and the constant influx of new games coming to Steam, Worming From Home stands as an unassuming addition to this line-up, releasing earlier today on Steam. Developed by two people, the physics-based simulation game tasks players with working from home albeit with a slight twist: you're a worm. Yet being a worm doesn't stop you from having big dreams and the ambition to see them brought to fruition. After getting a call from your boss, during which he tells you that after six years you're finally in line for a promotion to senior financial analyst, your worm-self must embark on a mission to up your work output and convince him you're ready for the added responsibility. Tasks will populate your task board, asking you to do things such as respond to emails from your colleagues or fill out spreadsheets. Some of these will require a bit of environmental exploration, such as a task that asked me to insert my height into an excel sheet, while some might force you to brush up on your math skills and pattern recognition; others might have strict deadlines, requiring you to navigate your environment with purpose and precision. You have to keep finding ways to accomplish your tasks no matter what and keep anyone from thinking you're incompetent--or discovering that you're a worm. And yet, you also have to maintain "worm-life balance." How do you do this? Well, when not working, you can exercise, read, shop, earn new, wormy cosmetics (hats, mainly), and use inside information to illegally game the stock market. You know. All normal, everyday things. You can also flirt with your co-workers, though, I don't know--that seems like a bad move when you're gunning for a management position, right?…

title: Let’s Stop Saying “Metroidvania”
description: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week. When we talk about something, we should talk about it in ways people can understand. You have to be deep in the "gamer" weeds to have any idea what "Metroidvania" means, though. You have to be familiar with not one but two different decades-old game series, and not just familiar with their names or generally aware of their existence, but knowledgeable about how they're designed and how they're actually played. And if you're that well-versed in Metroid and Castlevania, you know enough to know that neither truly invented this type of action game. And you know that the Castlevania games, the first of which didn't have any of the distinctive traits that define the genre that bears their name, didn't even popularize it, as Metroid did. (Yes, Vampire Killer and Simon's Quest both had Metroid-y elements, but the former wasn't open-ended enough and the latter was too open-ended and obtuse; it wasn't until Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, over a decade later, that Castlevania really jumped on board the 'Troid train.) Castlevania didn't adopt search-action mechanics until Symphony of the Night So either you have no idea what "Metroidvania" means, or you know that it's not even that accurate a term, and in either case, the solution is simple: Stop using it. I didn't have a lot of hard-and-fast rules during my 15 years editing the games section of a second-tier entertainment site that used to be a third-tier music magazine, but any of the dozens of writers who wrote for me knew of one big one: We tried as hard as possible to not use the word "metroidvania." It was never an absolute ban, and I'm sure if you go search whatever URL those articles currently live at, you'll find many pieces I edited that included it. But I definitely…

description: Withering Rooms was an unexpectedly devious and absorbing slice of dollhouse action-RPG horror. As such, I've been looking forward to Withering Realms, the standalone sort-of-sequel, which launches in early access today. The new game takes place in the 1920s, following the 'premature' end of World War 1 thanks to an occult catastrophe. You play a ghost child, clinging to the shoulders of a living marionette. The marionette is a real fright, its body a coatful of springs and hinges, its face a one-eyed rictus: it reminds me of certain scenes from Phil Tippett's stop motion masterpiece Mad God and also, of Curly from Mouthwashing. You wouldn't accept if that thing offered you a piggyback. But it is pretty handy in a fight. Read more

title: Playing Mass Effect-inspired RPG Exodus was an uncomfortably familiar space trip, despite some brilliant zero-G fights
description: Full disclosure: I did not get to play Exodus with the grumpy mecha octopus sniper. "Where’s the octopus sniper?", I whispered, confusion melting into sadness as the two other members of my space station infiltration team stepped forward under the support of their dull, seen-it-all-before vertebrae. No, it’s fine. It’s fine. I’d like to say that the demo’s shooting and roleplaying moments made up for the lack of squidmates. In some places, particularly when venturing back out into the vacuum, it actually did. But if Exodus really is going to occupy the Guns & Conversation space that Mass Effect is currently leaving vacant, I’d hope it’s holding much more in reserve, as the corridor battles and bland heroes I saw probably aren’t going to cut it.
